short_description: Consumer-facing appearance trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for male-pattern hair-loss tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing appearance trait with practical raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited hair-loss tendency and current visible hairline status for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with male-pattern baldness or patterned scalp-hair-loss tendency, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Male-pattern baldness tendency is presented here as a cautious relative appearance signal related to patterned scalp-hair loss over time, not as a direct statement about your current hairline or guaranteed future outcome. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic forecast of current or future hairline appearance.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
This source phenotype is specifically tied to male-pattern balding, so interpretation is less direct outside that phenotype context.
Real-world hair loss also depends strongly on age, sex hormones, medication use, grooming choices, hair transplantation or treatment history, and other non-modeled factors.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
